nodes.label: LSD_Engine
nodes.rationale: Takes public Bitsquid/Stingray ideas (data-oriented, data-driven, Lua) and adds an Unreal-like editor-first workflow; code is for new behaviour, never for hooking up content

nodes.label: Editor-first workflow (Unreal-style)
nodes.rationale: Import a file, find it in the Content Browser, open it in its own editor, wire it up by clicking

nodes.label: Proprietary licence / no GPL rule
nodes.rationale: Engine is all rights reserved; third-party code limited to MIT/BSD/zlib/FreeType, LGPL only separately linked

nodes.label: Data-oriented design principle
nodes.rationale: Entities are handles, components plain structs in packed arrays, systems loop over arrays, no inheritance

nodes.label: Reflection drives tools
nodes.rationale: Declare a struct once; Details panel, file format, undo, Lua access and Play copies come from generated TypeInfo

nodes.label: Clean-room rules
nodes.rationale: Ideas from public talks/blogs/books only; no Stingray/Bitsquid binaries, decompiled or leaked code, no on-screen code copying

nodes.label: lsd_stb target

nodes.rationale: Third-party implementation compiled with warnings silenced to keep 0-warning builds.

nodes.label: lsd_rhi target
nodes.rationale: Fails configure unless at least one backend is enabled; D3D12 forced off off-Windows; Vulkan shaders need the Vulkan SDK's DXC for SPIR-V, otherwise UI only.

nodes.label: Game target
nodes.rationale: Game.dll built from Source/*.c|cpp against the C API include only (LSD_GAME_API_INCLUDE), output to Binaries/ for hot reload.

nodes.label: reflect_gen_rejects_bad_header test (WILL_FAIL)
nodes.rationale: The generator must reject bad annotations with an error instead of producing code.

nodes.label: lsd_mcp target
nodes.rationale: Output next to lsd_editor.exe, where Editor Preferences > Plugins > Claude MCP points Claude Code.

nodes.label: lsd_reflect_gen target
nodes.rationale: Always built because engine targets depend on its generated reflection code.

nodes.label: Jolt Physics small API (bodies + CharacterVirtual)
nodes.rationale: No Jolt headers outside src/, so Jolt stays a private dependency of lsd_physics.

nodes.label: LuaJIT host-tool build (minilua -> DynASM -> buildvm)
nodes.rationale: Upstream LuaJIT has no CMake build, so it replays msvcbuild.bat / Makefile steps.

nodes.label: Permissive third-party licence policy
nodes.rationale: Only MIT/BSD/zlib; LGPL only separately linked; never GPL, because the engine is proprietary. Every library pinned to a tag.

hyperedges.label: Core engine design principles
Default editor layout: viewport, Outliner, Details, Content Browser, Editors dock
AI stack: navmesh, behaviour trees, perception
Ways to add visual script nodes (ScriptNode, C/C++, JavaScript)
Gameplay languages sharing the lsd API and script events
Editor default layout: menu bar, tabs, workspaces, viewport, Outliner, Details, Content Browser, Editors dock
Workspace tabs rearranging the Level editor (Modeling, Shading, Animation, Scripting, UI, Effects)
Gameplay languages sharing one binding list
Node libraries on script::Graph
JavaScript (QuickJS-ng) embedders
Modules using lsd_reflect() code generation
One RHI, three graphics backends
Per-asset editors opened as tabs in the Editors window
Profiling and diagnostics views
Editor settings windows (Editor Preferences, Project Settings, World Settings)
Level tab editor modes (3D Modeling, Landscape, PCG) sharing the viewport toolbar
Level modes with side panels painting into the level
C / C++ gameplay code workflow in the Tools menu
Data assets edited in the reflection-generated Details panel (Save / Revert)
Graph editors sharing one node-graph UI (Palette, wiring, shortcuts)
